claim: Velocity-pressure transforms reliable in the basin are much less stable below salt.
quote: velocity-pressure or velocity-stress relationships that may be quite reliable in the broader basin are found to be much less stable below salt (Hauser et al., 2013)

claim: Stress in salt is taken as isotropic and equal to the overburden, as in common basin-scale practice.
quote: consistent with common practice in both static and dynamic basin scale numerical models

claim: Overburden = seawater column + integral of a sediment density-depth trend a z^b + salt at constant density (Eq. 1).
quote: OBP = integral rho_seawater g dz + integral a z_bml^b g dz + integral rho_salt g dz

quote: a constant density of 2.17 g/cc (0.9408 psi/ft) was used for salt

quote: The rather narrow VES range of less than 4 MPa across a much larger range of overburden loads (75 MPa)

quote: Table 1, crestal leak, All: 0.0189 +/- 0.00103 MPa/m; -2.38 +/- 0.584 MPa

quote: This predicted trend of base-salt sediment pressures is substantially higher than the pressure gradients seen in regional data.
